title: lane-allocator-and-eviction-drivers-for-head-lane-mqa-compat
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: intermittent tail-latency spikes on multi-head MQA workloads and observable KV cache churn for variable sequence lengths. This PR introduces an adaptive 'lane allocator' inside the continuous-batching scheduler and a pluggable KV-eviction driver that cooperates with per-model kernel hints. Goals: reduce tail latency variance, lower redundant KV cache writes, and enable safer fallbacks for models with head-tiling quirks (Llama/Mistral/Qwen). Changes are targeted at runtime scheduler, KV cache, and model-specific hinting without changing public API.

Summary of changes and rationale: implement a lane allocator that shards in-flight tokens into soft lanes based on request latency budget and token-length distribution; lanes are soft concurrency groups which the scheduler uses to form micro-batches with tighter latency SLOs. Add a KV-eviction driver abstraction with three policies: time-based LRU, prefix-aware compact (retains recent prefixes), and lane-weighted eviction (prioritizes eviction from lanes with low expected reuse). Wire eviction decisions into the kernel selector so when eviction would drop KV slabs for a given model variant we prefer an alternative kernel path that does not rely on large KV slab residency.

Model-specific work: add per-model quirks table and unit tests with tuned defaults for Llama (head tiling + short-sequence prefix retention), Mistral (dense attention kernel prefers compact KV layout), Qwen (multi-query adaptations). Provide helper to derive lane target sizes from sequence length histograms collected in runtime metrics.

Performance: internal perf runs on a mixed 8xA100 cluster with synthetic chat load (80% short, 20% long seq). Results vs main:  p50 unchanged, p95 reduced by ~18%, p99 reduced by ~27%, mean KV write rate reduced by 22%, end-to-end token cost per 1k tokens down ~7% due to reduced re-computation and smarter batching.

Checklist: - [x] Scheduler lane allocator implementation and unit tests - [x] KV-eviction driver + integration tests - [x] Model quirks table and fallback kernel mappings - [x] Perf harness and benchmark results included - [x] Docs: internal DEVNOTES for ops tuning - [x] Backward-compatible; no public API changes

Notes on safety and rollout: default lane allocator is disabled by feature flag (runtime flag: lane_allocator_v1) in main and enabled in Dedicated perf ring. KV eviction default policy remains time-based LRU until ops flips lane-weighted eviction in controlled rollout. There is a metric-based automatic rollback hook if p95 increases beyond configured threshold.

review_thread: Diego Morales: Can you explain how lane boundaries handle heterogeneous request sizes? Is there risk of starvation for long-seq lanes?

Aisha Patel: Lanes are soft; we periodically rebalance using histogram-derived targets and a max-starve window (configurable). We also permit lane spillover if a lane cannot form a full micro-batch within the drain timeout.
Priya Singh: The eviction driver seems to add complexity; how do we validate correctness under high-concurrency?

Aisha Patel: Added integration test that simulates conflicting eviction and allocation; also added a correctness invariant check that validates KV references before kernel dispatch. See tests/kv/test_eviction_policies.cpp
Oliver Chen: Kernel selector fallback could change latency profile. Did you validate kernel selection doesn't regress p50?

Aisha Patel: Yes — selector prefers kernels with similar p50 characteristics and only selects fallback when eviction would otherwise break a KV-dependent kernel. Perf run included kernel-selection trace; attached to PR as artifacts.
merge_outcome: merged (squash) by Priya Singh after addressal of minor comment on time-window config; merge commit message summarizes perf and rollout notes
release_notes: Adaptive lane allocator and KV eviction drivers to reduce tail latency and KV churn on MQA/GQA workloads; opt-in via lane_allocator_v1 flag. Ops: see docs/DEVNOTES/lane-allocator.md for tuning steps.
